page.layout: One printed page. Running text in one column, with marginal notes in the left margin. A sliver of the neighbouring right-hand page at the far edge is not transcribed.

main_text.p: tio Domini. Respondet Cardinalis, intelligi, Merita noftra non esse ex nobis, sed ex Deo; ut ipse explicat, Serm. 68. in Cant. MERITA HABERE CURES: HABITA, DATA NO. VERIS. Sic ille. Nos vero potius ipsi Bernardo credimus: Idem ibid. ‘Majorem miserationem ne-mo habet, quàm ut animam suam ponat quis pro addictis morti & damnatis: meum proinde meritum miseratio Domini. Non planè sum meriti inops, quamdiu ille miserationum non fu-erit: quòd si misericordia Domini multa, multus nihilominus ego in meritis sum. Quid si multorum mihi conscius sim delictorum? Nempe UBI ABUNDAVIT DELICTUM, IBI SUPERABUNDAVIT GRATIA.’ Sic Bernardus, tantum de Meritis Christi erga se, in quae totus recumbit: quae tamen ausus est Bellarminus interpretari pro defensione etiam Meriti de Condigno ex æqualitate iustitiæ apud Deum; qui eâdem operâ lucem trans-mutet in tenebras.

head.i: Ejusdem Argumenti, ex Pontificiorum consensu, confirmatio.

main_text.head: SECT. IIII.
main_text.p: AUtores Pontificios bene multosCap. 7. Sect. 1.&c. antea{*} produximus, qui nobis astipulantes, remunerationem operum bonorum, ex Divina benignitate, acceptatione, dignatione, ac mi-sericordia

page.notes: The asterisk after "antea" and the note "Cap. 7. Sect. 1.&c." are matched by the mark "*". The mark before "Idem ibid." is not clearly visible, so the note carries no letter. The opening quotation mark before "Majorem" is faint and was read as a single quote. Possible printing or scan issues: "quàm ut" and "multa, multus" are read as printed but are slightly blurred. The line break "ac mi-/sericordia" is read from the scan. The running head "Cap. Io." is printed as a chapter marker and is kept with it.
